text:
incident-bot: Paging: HIGH - customer "Orion Health" experiencing 429s from Dedicated pool orion-prod-pool in us-west1. Errors spike ~17:46 UTC. Please acknowledge. Respond with :ack when taking lead.

jamie (oncall-sre): acked. jumping in. rough % of requests failing? any drop in latency?

maria (oncall-eng): seeing a flood of 429s tied to tenant_id=tenant.orion. Rate of 429s ~200r/s from that tenant, overall pool still has headroom but per-tenant throttle kicking. No latency spike, just rejection.

kevin (acct-rep): flagged by customer CS. They report production API errors impacting order ingest. They've been ramping new batch jobs today.

jamie (oncall-sre): ok. initial triage: confirm if this is a per-tenant quota enforcement (config) vs bug in pool routing. suhas, can you check dedicated pool tenant isolation rules?

suhas (infra): reading pool allocator logs now. Looks like tenant has hit "per-tenant-concurrency" soft limit set by contract. There's an enforcement shard returning 429s at the edge gw. Logs: ```
2026-06-05T17:45:12Z WARN tenant=tenant.orion reject=rate_limit key=tenant_concurrency current=128 limit=100
```

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated pool tenant 429s - steps: 1) validate contract limit 2) apply emergency lift if approved 3) monitor for noisy neighbor. Use /emergency-lift <tenant> <duration> <reason>.

maria (oncall-eng): Jamie, do we have authority to do an emergency lift for enterprise customers? Need confirmation from billing or ACCT rep per policy.

kevin (acct-rep): I can approve for Orion Health for 30 minutes while they finish backfill. They have an enterprise agreement but this is above committed concurrency. Approving emergency-lift 30m to unblock critical ingest.

jamie (oncall-sre): thanks Kevin. I'll perform emergency lift on the pool control plane. Will scope to tenant only, set duration 30m, and add audit tag. Applying now.

jamie (oncall-sre): running command: ```
# admin console CLI
redwoodctl quota override apply --tenant tenant.orion --pool orion-prod-pool --type concurrency --value 200 --duration 30m --reason "customer emergency - acct approved"
```

incident-bot: ACTION: emergency-lift requested by jamie (oncall-sre). Pending billing-bot confirmation.

billing-bot: Billing note auto-generated: Emergency override for tenant.orion, 30m. ACCT rep: kevin. No charge adjustments yet.

suhas (infra): I see the override apply job start: job_id=ovr-20260605-991. Patching enforcement tables now.

maria (oncall-eng): 17:50 UTC - customer telemetry shows 429 rate drop from 200r/s -> ~2r/s. Looks like the lift worked. Can we confirm ingress gateway stops tagging rejects?

jamie (oncall-sre): gateway logs show accepted tokens now. Sample: ```
2026-06-05T17:50:24Z INFO tenant=tenant.orion accept request_id=abc123
```

kevin (acct-rep): Confirmed with CS: Orion resumed ingest, they report ~15 minutes of backlog being processed. They thanked us.

maria (oncall-eng): leaving monitoring on for the 30m window. Also recommend a follow-up: 1) confirm why tenant spiked 128 concurrent, 2) offer customer suggested tuned committed concurrency, 3) ensure our autoscaling/guardrails catch this earlier.

jamie (oncall-sre): Agreed. I'll keep the lift active for 30m and will hand off to afternoon oncall at +20m for watch. @suhas can you open an infra ticket to investigate enforcement threshold behavior and whether a hard throttle was mis-evaluated?

suhas (infra): Will do. Creating INF ticket INF-4872 with logs and job_id=ovr-20260605-991.

ops-runbook-bot: NOTE: emergency-lift completed: will auto-expire at 18:20 UTC unless extended.

jamie (oncall-sre): tagging as postmortem candidate. Assigning root cause lead: maria. She'll coordinate with kevin for customer comms. Next steps recorded.

maria (oncall-eng): I'll draft a customer incident note summarizing impact, lift, and mitigation options. Also will include recommended contract amendment if they want higher burst capacity.

kevin (acct-rep): Please include estimates for monthly committed increase and delta for temporary bursts. I'll follow up with the customer.

jamie (oncall-sre): handoff to afternoon oncall in 15m. If anyone sees regressions please @jamie or escalate to incidents channel. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
